events.title: 애틀랜타에서 목사의 아들로 태어나다
events.title_en: Born in Atlanta to a pastor's family
events.description: 조지아주 애틀랜타에서 태어났다. 아버지와 외할아버지가 모두 침례교 목사였고, 그는 그 교회에서 자랐다.
events.description_en: He was born in Atlanta, Georgia. His father and his maternal grandfather were both Baptist ministers, and he grew up inside that church.

events.title: 모어하우스를 마치고 목사가 되다
events.title_en: He finished Morehouse and was ordained
events.description: 열다섯에 모어하우스 칼리지에 들어가 사회학을 공부했다. 졸업하던 해에 목사 안수를 받았다.
events.description_en: He entered Morehouse College at fifteen and studied sociology. In the year he graduated he was ordained a minister.

events.title: 크로저 신학교를 수석으로 마치다
events.title_en: He finished Crozer at the top of his class
events.description: 펜실베이니아의 크로저 신학교를 수석으로 마쳤다. 이 무렵 간디의 비폭력 저항을 읽고 자기 길로 삼았다.
events.description_en: He finished Crozer Theological Seminary in Pennsylvania at the top of his class. Around this time he read Gandhi on nonviolent resistance and made it his own road.

events.title: 코레타 스콧과 결혼하다
events.description: 성악을 공부하던 코레타 스콧과 결혼했다. 그녀는 뒤에 남편이 죽은 뒤로도 운동을 이어 갔다.
events.description_en: He married Coretta Scott, then studying voice. She carried the movement on long after her husband was killed.

events.title: 몽고메리 덱스터 애비뉴 교회를 맡다
events.title_en: He took the pulpit at Dexter Avenue in Montgomery
events.description: 앨라배마주 몽고메리의 덱스터 애비뉴 침례교회 담임목사가 되었다. 스물다섯이었다.
events.description_en: He became pastor of Dexter Avenue Baptist Church in Montgomery, Alabama. He was twenty-five.

events.title: 보스턴대에서 박사학위를 받다
events.title_en: He took his doctorate at Boston University
events.description_en: He took his doctorate in systematic theology at Boston University.

events.title: 몽고메리 버스 승차 거부를 이끌다
events.title_en: He led the Montgomery bus boycott
events.description: 로자 파크스가 백인에게 자리를 내주지 않아 체포되자 흑인 주민들이 버스를 타지 않기로 했다. 킹이 이 운동을 이끌었고, 사람들은 삼백여 일을 걸어 다녔다. 끝내 버스의 좌석 분리가 무너졌다.
events.description_en: When Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat, the city's Black residents agreed to stop riding the buses. King led them, and people walked for more than three hundred days. In the end the segregated seating fell.

events.title: 남부기독교지도자회의를 세우다
events.title_en: He founded the Southern Christian Leadership Conference
events.description: 남부의 흑인 교회들을 묶어 남부기독교지도자회의를 만들고 초대 의장이 되었다. 교회의 조직력을 운동의 뼈대로 삼았다.
events.description_en: He tied the Black churches of the South together into the Southern Christian Leadership Conference and became its first president. The church's organizing power became the frame of the movement.

events.title: 버밍햄 감옥에서 편지를 쓰다
events.title_en: He wrote a letter from the Birmingham jail
events.description: 앨라배마주 버밍햄에서 시위를 이끌다 체포되어 갇혔다. 감방에서 신문 여백에 편지를 썼다. 기다리라는 온건파 성직자들에게, 정의를 너무 오래 미루면 그것은 거부와 같다고 답했다.
events.description_en: He was arrested and jailed while leading demonstrations in Birmingham, Alabama. In the cell he wrote a letter in the margins of a newspaper. To the moderate clergymen who told him to wait, he answered that justice too long delayed is justice denied.

events.title: 워싱턴 행진에서 꿈을 말하다
events.title_en: He spoke of a dream at the March on Washington
events.description: 이십만 명이 넘는 사람들이 워싱턴에 모였다. 링컨 기념관 계단에서 그는 준비한 원고를 접고, 자기에게는 꿈이 있다고 말했다. 아이들이 피부색이 아니라 사람됨으로 평가받는 나라를 말한 것이다.
events.description_en: More than two hundred thousand people gathered in Washington. On the steps of the Lincoln Memorial he set aside his prepared text and said that he had a dream. He meant a country where his children would be judged by their character and not their skin.

events.title: 노벨 평화상을 받다
events.title_en: He received the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: 서른다섯에 노벨 평화상을 받았다. 상금은 전액 운동에 내놓았다. 같은 해 미국에서 민권법이 통과됐다.
events.description_en: He received the Nobel Peace Prize at thirty-five and gave the entire prize money to the movement. That same year the Civil Rights Act passed in the United States.

events.title: 셀마에서 몽고메리까지 걷다
events.title_en: He walked from Selma to Montgomery
events.description: 흑인의 투표 등록을 막는 앨라배마에 맞서 셀마에서 몽고메리까지 걸었다. 첫 시도는 다리 위에서 경찰봉에 막혔고, 그 장면이 전국에 방송됐다. 그해 투표권법이 통과됐다.
events.description_en: Against an Alabama that blocked Black voters from registering, he walked from Selma to Montgomery. The first attempt was beaten back with clubs on a bridge, and the whole country watched it on television. The Voting Rights Act passed that year.

events.title: 베트남 전쟁에 반대하고 지지를 잃다
events.title_en: He opposed the Vietnam War and lost support
events.description: 뉴욕 리버사이드 교회에서 베트남 전쟁을 정면으로 비판했다. 인종 문제에만 머물라던 언론과 정치권이 등을 돌렸고, 그는 가난한 사람들의 문제로 운동을 넓혀 갔다.
events.description_en: At Riverside Church in New York he attacked the Vietnam War head-on. The press and the politicians who wanted him to stay on race turned away from him, and he widened the movement toward the problems of the poor.

events.title: 멤피스에서 총에 맞아 죽다
events.title_en: He was shot dead in Memphis
events.description: 파업 중인 환경미화 노동자들을 돕겠다고 멤피스에 갔다. 로레인 모텔 발코니에 서 있다 총에 맞았다. 서른아홉이었다.
events.description_en: He went to Memphis to stand with the striking sanitation workers. He was shot while standing on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel. He was thirty-nine.
